scenes.title: 보이는 걷기 지시
lines: Here are two walks from Unreal’s Game Animation Sample. The figure on the left walks upright. The one on the right walks with bent knees. Watch the height of the head and the bend at the knees. Here is one way to turn “cautiously” into a usable direction. Keep the head from rising sharply as the feet trade support. The animator can now see exactly what to check.

scenes.title: 두 시점의 참고 포즈
lines: One method is to pose an articulated figure and photograph it. Simplify the background and mark the hands and feet to make a reference. Here, we view an Unreal mannequin’s first step from two angles. At the same instant the feet can overlap from one angle, while the other angle reveals which foot is leading. For the reference pose, choose the angle that separates the feet and note which foot should carry the weight and where the body should face. Put that still beside the finished motion to see how much of the original intent comes through.

scenes.title: 정지 동작의 지지발
lines: Compare the last step in these two stops. One clip uses the left foot as its reference, the other the right. In the final pose both are standing still, so it is easy to miss the difference. Keep the foot position before the stop beside the settled pose. The animator can then tell which leg is meant to receive the weight.

scenes.title: 방향 전환 검수
lines: Finally, watch the change of direction at normal speed. Compare left and right turns from the same camera. You can read how the torso follows the planted foot. When requesting a revision, go beyond “make it more natural.” Specify which footfall should coincide with the change of facing.
